description: This bar chart illustrates the relative performance of different parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods across four distinct data distribution scenarios: Increasing, Uniform, Decreasing, and Bottleneck. The horizontal axis displays the names of the PEFT methods, labeled “Increasing”, “Uniform”, “Decreasing”, and “Bottleneck”, and the bars are arranged alphabetically. The vertical axis, labeled “Performance”, represents a linear scale ranging from 0 to 1, with tick marks at intervals of 0.2. Each data distribution scenario is represented by a set of five light green bars. For the “Increasing” distribution, the bar heights range from approximately 0.2 to 0.8. The “Uniform” distribution shows bars with heights between approximately 0.3 and 0.7. For the “Decreasing” distribution, the bar heights range from approximately 0.7 to 0.2. Finally, the “Bottleneck” distribution displays bars with heights between approximately 0.4 and 0.6. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, outlining, or annotation.
